note: Standard headers a hot header must not reach (docs/design/build-performance.md#include-budget). Each entry includes `include` in a probe unit compiled with the command of `flags_of` (a unit of the configuration's compile database, matched by path suffix) and the compiler's include listing; a forbidden header anywhere in the probe's include closure fails, with the chain that reached it. `forbid` applies to every compiler, `forbid_gnu` to GCC and Clang only (on MSVC the C runtime's <wchar.h> includes <intrin.h> and with it <immintrin.h> in nearly every unit, whatever the project includes). The costs are the 2026-10-18 profiles (docs/bench/2026-10-18-build-speed-compile-time.md).

entries.why: in about 1,400 units; libstdc++'s <iterator> brings the stream-buffer iterators and with them <streambuf>, <ios_base> and the locale classes (array.hpp 381 s of Clang front end before it was dropped)
hash.hpp and hash_map.hpp reach about 830 units; MSVC's <functional> brings <unordered_map> (130 s of MSVC front end)
the set shares hash_map.hpp's key equality (DefaultEqual), not std::equal_to's <functional>
in about 240 units; two std::min calls had brought <algorithm>
the scalar exp and log family; its cores live in crd/math/exp_log_core.hpp, apart from the AVX2 twins whose <immintrin.h> cost about 0.34 s in each Clang unit
the one-include math surface, in about 640 units; through its transcendental functions it had brought the SIMD backend (simd/backend.hpp 275 s of Clang front end in 818 units)
its Vec4f and Vec8f overloads only name the vector types, so the types are declared, not included; crd/hesap/complex.hpp brings it into about 330 units

the batch small-float conversions behind every crd-hesap-tensor storage dtype; their F16C and AVX2 bodies are per-level kernel units (SIMD-DISPATCH), so the header brings no intrinsics header to its consumers
the counter RNG of hesap-opt, hesap-tensor and the stats samplers; its bulk fill runs the per-level stats kernels (SIMD-DISPATCH), so the header brings no intrinsics header to its consumers
every unit of crd/hesap/stats/stats.hpp; its bulk fill runs the per-level stats kernels (SIMD-DISPATCH), so the header brings no intrinsics header

the special functions of hesap-stats, hesap-quadrature and the distributions; the Lanczos lgamma and tgamma batches run the per-level special kernels (SIMD-DISPATCH), so the header brings no intrinsics header to its consumers (its <complex> reaches <sstream>, as crd/math/cmath.hpp does)

the GEMM packing and block dispatch behind gemm, syrk and the supernodal factor walks; its f64 and f32 register tiles are per-level dense kernels (SIMD-DISPATCH), so the header brings no intrinsics header to its consumers
the SELL-C-sigma spmv of the sparse LinearOps and Krylov solvers; its f64 and f32 bodies are per-level sparse kernels (SIMD-DISPATCH), so the header brings no intrinsics header to its consumers

the FFT plan of hesap-dsp, the spectral interpolants, the wavelets and the fft CLI; its transform runs the per-level fft kernels (SIMD-DISPATCH), so the header brings no intrinsics header and no generated codelet to its consumers
the einsum and TTGT transpose; its f32 tile bodies are per-level tensor kernels (SIMD-DISPATCH), so the header brings no intrinsics header to its consumers

the storage dtypes and SR converts; the SR draws run the per-level tensor kernels' Philox block loop and the narrowers the crd-math kernels (SIMD-DISPATCH), so the header brings no intrinsics header to its consumers
the broadcast binary ops run the per-level tensor kernels (SIMD-DISPATCH), so the header brings no intrinsics header, the baseline's SSE2 ones included, to its consumers
Tier D (reduce.hpp and the axis folds) runs the per-level tensor kernels (SIMD-DISPATCH), so neither header brings an intrinsics header to its consumers
einsum's direct products run the per-level tensor kernels and its GEMMs the dense ones (SIMD-DISPATCH), so the header brings no intrinsics header to its consumers
the batched GEMM, factorizations and solves run the per-level tensor kernels (SIMD-DISPATCH), so the header brings no intrinsics header to its consumers

every test unit; with the two Catch2 patches (catch2-chrono-stringmaker-opt-in, catch2-clock-chrono-subset) the assertion path no longer reaches <chrono>, which was the build's most expensive header (575 s MSVC, 633 s Clang)

Catch2's own units (in its unity batches, or one per source with CRD_CATCH2_UNITY=OFF) reach the patched copies first, through a plain -I ahead of Catch2's source directory, so the whole program has one definition of every Catch2 entity; the unpatched header includes <chrono> unconditionally
